description: Known exact values of M(n) for the Erdős minimum overlap problem. M(n) = min over equipartitions A ⊔ B = [2n], |A|=|B|=n, of max_k |A ∩ (B+k)|. lim_{n→∞} M(n)/n = µ ∈ [0.380128, 0.380871].

sources.wikipedia_handwiki: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_overlap_problem — lists M(n) for n=1..15, attributed to Haugland (1996, 2016) and Guy 'Unsolved Problems in Number Theory' (2004).
sources.our_brute_force: lp_research_state/code/_brute_force_Mn_extended.py — branch-and-bound + reflection symmetry, agrees with published n=2..15 and extends to n=18. Data: Mn_optimizers_large.json.

notes: M(n)/n is monotone-non-strict only in the lim inf sense. Individual ratios fluctuate (n=15: 0.40, n=18: 0.44).

No published table extends past n=15. The literature on UB for µ uses continuous step-function constructions (Haugland 2016 51-step, AlphaEvolve 95-step, TTT-Discover/Together 600-step) — these do not produce integer M(n) values.
Together's repo (/tmp/together_repo/erdos-minimum-overlap) contains only step-function constructions, no M(n) tables.
Brute force timing growth: n=16 → 17 → 18 = 54s → 66s → 664s. n=18→19 projected ~5000-7000s, well beyond the 30 min budget; n=20 would be a multi-hour overnight job.
